nuclearPlants.name: North Anna Power Station
nuclearPlants.operator: Dominion Energy (owners Dominion Virginia Power 88.4%, Old Dominion Electric Cooperative 11.6%)
nuclearPlants.notes: Louisa County, near Mineral; two operating units. Distance is a straight-line calculation from Henrico's listed center (37.55, -77.40) to the plant, not an official figure. Henrico is outside the 10-mile plume zone. The 50-mile ingestion zone circle covers most of Henrico by that math (western edge about 29 mi; far eastern edge about 53 mi), but no opened source lists Henrico as an official ingestion-zone locality. 10-mile/50-mile definitions: NRC planning-zones page; VDEM says the 10-mile and 50-mile zones exist for both plants and does not list localities.

nuclearPlants.name: Surry Power Station
nuclearPlants.notes: Surry County on the James River across from Jamestown; two units. Straight-line distance from Henrico's listed center; eastern Henrico is about 34 mi away, western edge about 62 mi. So parts of eastern/central Henrico fall inside a 50-mile circle by geometry, but no opened source lists Henrico as an official ingestion-zone locality. Henrico is outside the 10-mile plume zone.

potassiumIodide.summary: KI (potassium iodide) is an over-the-counter supplement that helps protect the thyroid from radioactive iodine released in an unlikely reactor accident. It does not protect against other radiation. Not every accident releases radioiodine.
potassiumIodide.virginiaDistribution: VDH says the NRC supplied KI to states for the 10-mile plume zone around plants. VDH will recommend KI for the public at Evacuation Assembly Centers when the projected thyroid dose exceeds 5 rem; it is also available to emergency workers. The page does not describe a program that hands KI to residents in advance, and Henrico is outside the 10-mile zone. Supply lot TU905A expires 10/31/2029. Don't flush expired tablets.

waterUtility.provider: Henrico County Department of Public Utilities
waterUtility.sourceWater: James River (surface water). Henrico's new Cobbs Creek Reservoir ($280M) can supply 75 million gallons per day of raw James River water (WTVR, Jan 2025).
waterUtility.treatmentPlant: Two sources: Henrico's own water treatment facility in the west end, and treated water bought from the City of Richmond's plant (about 27% of that plant's output under a 2018 supply plan; agreement runs to 2040) per WTVR Jan 12, 2025. Henrico's own plant's official name/capacity was not confirmed from an opened source.
waterUtility.boilAdvisoryInfo: Countywide boil advisories are sent through Henrico's Everbridge alert system (opt-in; sign up at alert.henrico.gov). In January 2025 the county's alert list held 226,512 contacts, only 79,863 had opted in, 95,707 were outdated, and more than 90,000 countywide alerts bounced as undeliverable. Keep your own contact info current and also watch henrico.gov and local news.
waterUtility.notes: January 2025: Richmond's water plant lost power and its backup power could not keep it running. Henrico, which depends on Richmond's plant for part of its supply, disconnected from the shared system and tried to move water from its west-end plant to the east end; about 24,000 customers lost service at the peak and a Sandston water main break left thousands more without water. A boil advisory covering Henrico, Hanover and Richmond was lifted Saturday Jan 11 (WTVR; the county's lift notice itself returned 403). The county manager said 'we must do better' and a third-party review was to start the following Monday. VDEM's preparedness guidance is a supply kit with at least 3 days of food, water and medication.

hazards.localNotes: Henrico is inland; the main risks are wind-driven tree and power-line damage, flash flooding from heavy rain, tornadoes spun off by landfalling storms, and James River surge/flooding. Hurricane Isabel (Sept 2003) left more than 2 million people without power and about $1 billion in Virginia damage, with surge up the James River (12 On Your Side). Atlantic season is June 1-Nov 30, peak mid-Aug to late Oct; a Watch means a storm is possible within 48 hours. Flood insurance has a 30-day waiting period. Keep generators outside, 20 ft from the house. VDEM's 'Know Your Zone' evacuation program covers coastal localities, not Henrico.

Dominion Energy says about 0.25 inch of ice can be enough to knock out power, and ahead of the Jan 2026 storm it warned of multi-day outages statewide. The Richmond metro was largely spared in Jan 2026 (about 1,000 outages per search results). Never run a generator, grill or camp stove indoors or in a garage; replace CO-detector batteries yearly. Check 511Virginia.org before driving. Dominion recommends having medications filled in advance and power for medical devices ready before a storm.

On Sept 17, 2018 (remnants of Florence) an EF-1 with 90-95 mph winds ran about 3.8 miles from the City of Richmond into the Tuckahoe area of Henrico, uprooting trees onto houses and tearing HVAC units off a West End church roof; no injuries. Watch = tornadoes possible; Warning = take shelter now in the lowest interior room away from windows. Mobile homes are not safe.

VDEM defines extreme heat as above 90 F for 2-3 days with humidity. Henrico opens cooling centers during heat waves (July 3-4, 2026: Libbie Mill Library and Eastern Henrico Recreation Center) and the Salvation Army shelter on Chamberlayne Ave opens at 92 F. Fans do not cool people above 95 F.

The NWS/MARFC record for the James River near Richmond (the Westham gage, which sits in Henrico) covers 1816 to present with 193 flood events and a flood stage of 12 feet. Floods are most common in March (36) and April (27), then February (22) and January (20); July has had only 1. The report (created 1/23/2020) shows the last flood as 4/22/2019. Flash flooding: 6 inches of moving water can knock you down, 1 foot can float a car. Check your property in the Virginia Flood Risk Information System.

Older pages reference henricoalert.org.
